title: The Feynman Technique
summary: Master any topic by teaching it in simple language.
content:
Step 1: Choose a concept.
Step 2: Explain it to a hypothetical 10-year-old using clear, simple vocabulary.
Step 3: Identify knowledge gaps where your explanation stumbles.
Step 4: Review your primary source notes and refine the explanation with intuitive analogies.

title: Spaced Repetition Schedule
summary: Review material right before you are likely to forget it.
content: Optimal review intervals for long-term retention: Review immediately after session (Day 0), 24 hours later (Day 1), Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 30. This permanently shifts information into semantic long-term memory.

title: Active Recall vs. Passive Re-reading
summary: Testing yourself produces up to 300% better retention than re-reading.
content: Close your textbook or notes. On a blank sheet of paper, write down or diagram everything you can remember about the topic. Compare with notes to spot missing elements. Quizzing forces neural pathways to strengthen.

title: Pomodoro Flow Optimization
summary: 25 minutes of deep focus followed by 5 minutes of true sensory rest.
content: During focus intervals, eliminate all notifications and browser tabs. During the 5-minute break, avoid scrolling social media or checking emails—stand up, stretch, hydrate, and rest your eyes looking at a distant object.

title: Interleaving Study Subjects
summary: Switch between related topics rather than mass-blocking a single topic for 6 hours.
content: Instead of studying Calculus for 5 hours straight, spend 90 minutes on Calculus, switch to Data Structures for 90 minutes, then Physics. Interleaving improves discrimination skills and problem-solving flexibility.

title: Sleep and Memory Consolidation
summary: Deep sleep (SWS) and REM sleep are when the brain converts short-term memories into permanent knowledge.
content: All-nighters severely degrade cognitive recall and analytical ability. Aim for 7 to 8.5 hours of uninterrupted sleep, particularly during exam weeks. Avoid bright blue screens 45 minutes before sleep.

title: The Blurting Method
summary: Rapid retrieval practice for comprehensive syllabus coverage.
content: Pick a syllabus subtopic. Set a timer for 10 minutes. Write down every formula, definition, diagram, and keyword you recall without looking. Use a red pen to fill in anything missed from your notes.

title: Eat the Frog First
summary: Tackle your hardest or most dreaded subject in your first morning study block.
content: Willpower and neurochemical focus reserves are highest early in the day. Complete the most cognitively demanding topic before noon to create momentum and reduce procrastination anxiety.
